title: Times Square Rings In Diwali With Diya Countdown and Concert
excerpt: The 11th Diwali at Times Square filled Broadway on October 24 with a bazaar, dance showcases and a diya-lighting countdown on the One Times Square tower, two weeks before Diwali itself on November 8.
body:
• Diwali at Times Square held its 11th edition on Saturday, October 24, 2026, closing with a Diya Lighting Ceremony and a countdown on the One Times Square Ball Drop Tower screen.
  • Kanika Kapoor, Raja Kumari, Rishi Singh and Shanmukha Priya headlined the Light Up Times Square Concert, after a day that included a Diwali Bazaar, a Kids Zone and the “Colors of India and America” dance showcase.
  • The festival is an early celebration: Diwali itself falls on Sunday, November 8, 2026, and the holiday has been a New York City public school holiday since 2023.
  • Admission was free, and Colors TV, the festival’s media partner, broadcast the celebration for viewers who could not attend in person.

Times Square marked Diwali on Saturday, October 24, with the 11th edition of Diwali at Times Square, a day-long festival that ended with dignitaries lighting a diya as a countdown ran on the Ball Drop Tower screen at One Times Square. The celebration, organized by Sammaan For All and presented by P&G and Tide and Toyota, brought a Diwali Bazaar, cultural performances and a headline concert to the blocks around Broadway, according to the organizer’s announcement carried by PR Newswire.

A Countdown Borrowed From New Year’s Eve

The evening ceremony is the festival’s signature moment. After an afternoon of performances, dignitaries joined together for the Diya Lighting Ceremony, with the countdown displayed on the same tower screen that counts down the New Year’s Eve ball drop, leading into the Light Up Times Square Concert. Secret NYC, previewing the event, described it as the largest Diwali festival outside India and noted that New York City has partnered with the festival since 2024. The city declared October 29, 2023, “Diwali at Times Square Day.”

The wider program began a day earlier. An awards and gala dinner on October 23 at Tribeca 360 honored Indian Americans for contributions to philanthropy, innovation, medicine and entrepreneurship, according to IndiaWest. On October 24, the Kids Zone offered diya painting, rangoli activities and Bollywood dance lessons, alongside product sampling and educational displays from festival partners.

Concert Lineup and a Day of Programming

The afternoon showcase, “Colors of India and America,” featured Indian, Indo-Caribbean and Hispanic dance groups. The closing concert lineup mixed Bollywood and Indian-American acts: Filmfare Award-winning singer Kanika Kapoor, Grammy-nominated rapper Raja Kumari, Indian Idol 13 winner Rishi Singh and Indian Idol 12 finalist Shanmukha Priya, along with singer-rapper Sparsh Shah, known as “Purhythm,” New York’s Kunal Lamba and New Jersey singer Saanvi Nacha.

The Consulate General of India in New York hosted a press conference for the festival on October 14, where Deputy Consul General Vishal Harsh expressed support for the celebration. In a message, Consul General Binaya S. Pradhan framed the festival as part of the relationship between the two countries.

"Diwali celebrates the triumph of light over darkness, knowledge over ignorance, and hope over despair. I commend Sammaan For All-Diwali At Times Square for bringing communities together in one of the world's most iconic public spaces to share the joy of this festival."

— Binaya S. Pradhan, Consul General of India in New York

Neeta Bhasin, the founder and creator of Diwali at Times Square, said the event aims to instill pride in South Asian American youth in their heritage and to promote the values of art, culture and togetherness associated with Diwali, according to IndiaWest. Sponsors included Gopi as platinum sponsor, Xoom by PayPal as gold sponsor and the State Bank of India.

Why the Festival Lands Before Diwali Itself

The October 24 date is deliberate. Diwali in 2026 falls on Sunday, November 8, so the Times Square celebration functions as a public kickoff two weeks ahead of the holiday, on a weekend when a street festival can draw a full-day crowd. The pattern is consistent across the United States, where the largest public Diwali events are typically scheduled on the weekends before the day itself, while November 8 is kept for home and temple observances. Diwali has been a New York City public school holiday since 2023, though in 2026 it falls on a Sunday.

What Comes Next

For diaspora families in the New York area, the Times Square festival is the season’s opener rather than its finale. Community and temple celebrations continue through the November 8 holiday, and Colors TV’s broadcast of the Times Square program extends the event to viewers outside the city. The festival’s second decade now rests on a fixed formula — bazaar, cultural showcase, diya countdown, concert — that has made Diwali part of Times Square’s annual calendar alongside its better-known New Year’s Eve countdown.
